clue.text: Show on air — we'll abominate it unfairly?

definitions.text: Show on air — we'll abominate it unfairly?

indicators.note: treated unfairly, the clue's letters are jumbled out of their proper order

parts.words: Show on air — we'll abominate it

explanation.surface: A grumpy viewer vows to hate a broadcast programme no matter how it turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: All twenty-four letters of 'Show on air we'll abominate it' rearrange to the quiz title; the whole clue is the definition too, a sour viewer's view of the show.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running television quiz offering a million-pound top prize is a show on air that some viewers love to hate.

clue.text: Strongly built cathedral captured on film

parts.note: Wells in Somerset is a cathedral city, standing for its cathedral
ET is Spielberg's film about the extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A sturdy cathedral has been caught on camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-set person has a sturdy, solid build, a synonym of strongly built.

clue.text: Old company has iron chucked in river

indicators.note: the jumbled iron goes in between the two other pieces
chucked about, the letters of iron are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An old firm dumps scrap iron in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chucked' scrambles the word iron, and 'in' places the result between the abbreviations for old and company.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is a major South American river flowing through Venezuela.

clue.text: A seductive film star with wrinkle overcome by dread?

parts.note: Mae West was the famously suggestive Hollywood star
a ruck is a crease or wrinkle in cloth

explanation.surface: A sultry screen goddess frets about a crease in her costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Being awestruck means filled with awe, a feeling that mixes wonder with dread; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Rising cricketer gets pair? Not to be mentioned

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
a pair in cricket is two ducks, scores of nought, shown as two Os

explanation.surface: A batsman on the up is about to bag a pair, something nobody should mention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns BAT into TAB. A pair is getting out for nought (a duck) in both innings of a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo subject is forbidden, one that is not to be mentioned in polite company.

clue.text: Paint a beautiful valley, artist!

parts.note: the Vale of Tempe in Greece is a classically celebrated beautiful valley
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist is urged to paint a lovely valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Tempe is a gorge in Thessaly praised by ancient poets for its beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a paint made by binding pigment with egg yolk.

clue.text: French king, one emerging in good Parisian garment

indicators.note: the shortened king's name sits in the French word for good

parts.note: bon is French for good

indicators.note: one, the letter I, comes out of the king's name

parts.note: Louis was the name of many French kings

explanation.surface: A French monarch steps out wearing a fine Parisian outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one emerging' takes I (one) out of LOUIS, leaving LOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A blouson is a short, loose jacket gathered at the waist, a kind of garment.

clue.text: See 1 across
Junk emails ushering in a sense of unease

indicators.note: the jumbled emails let the letter a inside them
to junk is to scrap, so the word emails is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A flood of spam leaves the reader feeling uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk' rearranges EMAILS to MALISE, and 'ushering in' puts A inside it after MAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a vague feeling of discomfort or unease, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Get rid of useless papers, including rejected Dandy

indicators.note: the papers word holds the turned dandy inside it

parts.note: bumf is slang for useless paperwork

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the dandy word is read backwards

parts.note: a fop is a dandy, a man vain about dress

explanation.surface: Someone clears out pointless paperwork, including a returned copy of a comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the dandy word backwards inside the paperwork slang. The Dandy was also a British children's comic, the false trail here.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump off is slang for to kill, that is, to get rid of someone.

clue.text: Mad myth's 'ere — at first reader is misled?

definitions.text: Mad myth's 'ere — at first reader is misled?

indicators.note: misled means led astray, so the letters wander into a different order

explanation.surface: A tabloid story so mad that the first reader is surely being fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'mad myth's ere at first reader' rearrange into the famous 1986 Sun front-page headline about the comedian, a made-up story.
explanation.definitionFit: The notorious invented tabloid headline about a comedian was a mad myth that misled its readers.

clue.text: Survive as the tenth batsman to be dismissed?

definitions.text: the tenth batsman to be dismissed?
definitions.meaning: in cricket the tenth wicket to fall ends the innings, so that batsman is the final one out

explanation.surface: A cricketer hopes to hang on rather than be the last wicket to fall.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket innings ends when ten of the eleven batsmen are out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to endure until the end of a hard period, so survive is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Manage to find poetry in Old English

indicators.note: the poetry word goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A scholar manages to locate poems written in Old English.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee a project is to supervise or manage it.

clue.text: Paint room — what's first action to be incorporated?

indicators.note: what is incorporated is held within the body of the words before

explanation.surface: A decorator asks what job comes first when doing up a room.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an opening section, the first part of a piece of music or a show.

clue.text: A foreign place found by woman and daughter not on schedule

parts.note: un is French for a
PL is an abbreviation for place, as in street names
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Two travelling women stumble on a foreign spot that was never on the itinerary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unplanned was not scheduled or arranged in advance.

clue.text: Writer has marks with stars and mystical symbol

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a tag marks or labels something
the Ram is Aries, the constellation and sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An author covers a page with marks, stars and occult signs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ram is the group of stars known as Aries.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagram is a five-pointed star used as a magical or occult sign.

clue.text: American and Jamaican music amidst banner waving

indicators.note: the music sits in the middle of the jumbled letters
a waving banner moves about, so its letters are shuffled

parts.note: ska is a Jamaican music style

explanation.surface: A reggae band plays beneath a flag fluttering in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waving' scrambles banner, and 'amidst' places the Jamaican music inside it, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nebraskan comes from Nebraska, a US state, so is an American.

clue.text: Pomposity of doctor in swanking

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go inside the boasting word

parts.note: to swank is to show off, so swanking is boasting; boast stands for the act
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A doctor shows off with self-important talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is pompous, inflated language, so it means pomposity.

clue.text: Mortar mixed to seal in fine sculpture maybe

indicators.note: the jumbled mortar letters enclose the abbreviation
mortar is mixed, so its letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A builder stirs up mortar to fill joints in a fine statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' scrambles mortar, and 'to seal in' places the fine abbreviation inside, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculpture is one example of an art form, hence the maybe.

clue.text: Rob's half-hearted flick through magazine?

indicators.note: the word loses half of its middle pair of Fs

parts.note: to riffle a magazine is to flick through its pages

explanation.surface: Rob idly leafs through a glossy magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' drops one of the two central Fs from RIFFLE. A rifle also has a magazine, the misleading picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search it and steal from it, to rob.

clue.text: Cast out, ma tried to get let in again

indicators.note: cast out of their arrangement, the letters of ma tried are reordered

explanation.surface: Thrown out of the house, Mum tried to get back inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit someone is to let them back in, admitting again.

clue.text: Female mocker makes one weaker

parts.note: to rail at is to scold or mock, so a railer is one who mocks

explanation.surface: A woman who taunts others ends up worse off.
explanation.definitionFit: Frailer is the comparative of frail, meaning more feeble, that is weaker.

clue.text: Spanish lady entertaining dull residents

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the lady's name holds the other piece

parts.note: Ines is a Spanish woman's name
mat or matt means dull, not glossy

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman plays host to some boring housemates.
explanation.definitionFit: Inmates are those residing in an institution, such as a prison or asylum.

clue.text: Woman with oomph given a brief cheer

parts.note: SA is sex appeal, also called oomph
rah is a short form of hurrah

explanation.surface: A glamorous woman gets a quick round of applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah is a common woman's given name.

clue.text: Very hard man starting things off, a little worker?

parts.note: Adam was the first man in the Bible, beginning humankind
the ant is the classic small worker insect

explanation.surface: A tough man launches a project and needs a tiny helper.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant historically named a legendary unbreakable stone; as an adjective it means unyielding.

clue.text: Woman associated with crime, not half full of love and charm

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name

indicators.note: the halved crime word is filled with the letter for love
only half of the crime word is kept

parts.note: murder is a crime
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman linked to a killing, enchanted and lovestruck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' cuts MURDER to MUR, and 'full of' sets O inside it, making MOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour is to fill with love, to captivate or charm.

clue.text: One complaining? No good, one making a noise

indicators.note: G is the abbreviation for good, and no good means it is taken away

parts.note: a grumbler complains

explanation.surface: A moaner, useless and loud, disturbs everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumbler makes a deep rolling noise, like thunder or a stomach.

clue.text: See 10
